transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate your time. 

I hope I'm explaining this right, but... well, for the past year or so, I've just been noticing this little issue at work. I mean, it's probably not a huge deal, I still run my company fine and everything, but... I don't know, the smallest things seem to catch my attention before I can even stop it. 

Like, if my phone buzzes, or if somebody just walks past my office door, or even if I just have a completely random thought pop up—like about my in-laws or something—suddenly I'm completely pulled off whatever I was working on. It's just a bit frustrating, but I wanted to see if that's something you could help me with? Does that make sense to be here for that?
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or getting distracted when you were a child?

Oh, um... well, I guess if I really think about it... yeah, maybe a little bit? I mean, I wasn't a bad kid or anything! I just... I had a lot of energy, you know? 

I remember teachers would sometimes move my desk around. Not because I was trying to cause trouble, I just... I liked talking to people. And sometimes I'd get up to throw something away or sharpen a pencil without really asking first, which I guess they didn't love. Or I'd get so excited to answer a question that I'd just sort of say it before they finished asking. 

But that's pretty normal for a kid, right? Just being eager? I hope that doesn't sound like I was a problem student or anything.
Do these attention problems happen only at work, or also in other parts of your life?

Well, I guess... um, it's not *just* at work, if I'm being completely honest. But it's nothing terrible! Just little things, mostly. 

Like, at home, I'll tell my wife I'm going to call the insurance guy, or maybe pick up something we need for the house. And then... well, days will go by, and she'll ask me about it, and I'll realize I just honestly forgot all about it. I don't mean to, of course! I just get caught up in other things and it completely slips my mind. 

I know it probably frustrates her a little, which I feel bad about. But a lot of guys are a little forgetful around the house, right? I'm sure it's pretty common... I just hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad husband or anything.
Before age 12, did you often have the same kinds of attention or hyperactive/impulsive problems at school or at home?

Um, yeah, actually... I think that's kind of what I was trying to say earlier? Like, when I was in elementary school, definitely before I was twelve. That was when the teachers were always moving my seat around because I talked a bit too much... or, you know, when I'd get up without asking or blurt out the answers before they even finished the question. 

Looking back, it was all right around that age. At home, my parents just thought I was, well, a typical energetic boy. I really wasn't trying to be difficult or anything! I just... I had a lot of enthusiasm, I guess. I always meant well. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information here...

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, with childhood onset before age 12 and persistent symptoms into adulthood. He reports distractibility, forgetfulness, and difficulty sustaining attention across work and home settings, along with childhood hyperactive/impulsive features (talking excessively, leaving seat/getting up without asking, blurting out answers). Symptoms are longstanding and cause interpersonal and occupational frustration, consistent with ADHD.
